key_insight: Dead-end pores are not always hydraulically irrelevant: when they are densely distributed along flow paths, they can increase a porous medium’s intrinsic permeability through localized junction-scale interactions.
engineering_relevance: Permeability predictions and porous-media design should account for dead-end pore architecture—not just porosity and pore-size statistics—when estimating flow performance in soils, rocks, filters, and engineered porous materials.
method: Pore-scale flow simulations on multiple dead-end pore configurations
Compared heterogeneous arrangements, controlled granular assemblies, and a minimal single-channel model
Isolated effects of dead-end pore density, depth, and orientation while preserving the transmitting network
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent simulation evidence that increasing dead-end pore density along percolating paths enhances permeability, while pore depth and junction orientation have negligible effects.
watch_item: The proposed effective formulation is based on idealized pore-scale structures, so real materials may require calibration before direct engineering use.
paper_title: Pore-shape and its spatial organization control intrinsic permeability of porous media
